title: Cunning Strategies
content: Cunning is about being observant and understanding others' motivations. Key practices include maintaining information asymmetry by asking more questions than talking, and understanding incentives by identifying what others truly want rather than what they say they want. This allows for more strategic positioning and predicting behavior.
raw_text:
Okay, straight answer — cunning is mostly just thinking one step ahead while others aren't thinking at all.

Most people are on autopilot. They react, they're predictable, they show their hand without realizing it. Cunning people just... pay attention when others don't.

Here's what it actually looks like in practice:

Information asymmetry — know more than you reveal. Ask questions, listen more than you talk. The person who talks most in a negotiation almost always loses. People will tell you everything if you just stay quiet and curious.

Understand incentives — always ask: what does this person actually want? Not what they're saying, but what they *want*. Once you know that, you can predict their behavior and position yourself accordingly.
